source_title: Corporate Giants Are Staying on Top Longer. Should They Feel Safe?
figure_ref: Exhibit 1 — Leadership Has Been Locking In, but the Degree Varies by Sector
chart_key: https://www.bcg.com/publications/2026/market-leaders-staying-on-top-longer#Exhibit 1 — Leadership Has Been Locking In, but the Degree Varies by Sector
key_message: 시장가치 상위 기업의 가치 가중 교체율은 1990–2004년 중앙값 24%에서 2005–2025년 13%로 낮아졌지만 업종별 차이가 크므로 산업별 고착화 위험을 따로 평가해야 한다.

data_spec.metric: Giant churn: entrants' market cap as % of sector top-ten market cap
data_spec.denominator: Top ten firms' market capitalization in each industry
data_spec.observations: 15 visually digitized industry points, ±3 percentage points; narrative medians 24%,13% reported separately
data_spec.population: US-listed top 2,000 market-cap firms; data from S&P Capital IQ

data_recipe: Collect top-ten companies by sector and market cap at five-year intervals
Identify companies entering the top ten relative to the preceding period
Sum entrant market cap divided by total top-ten cap
Take median of five-year observations separately in each era
Plot sector-level pairs, retaining point digitization uncertainty
message_conditions: Sector classification must be consistent across eras
Point coordinates are digitized estimates, not reported underlying observations
Omitted private companies and non-US-only listings limit generalization
diff_notes: Original public low-resolution Exhibit 1 opened; point coordinate readings approximate. Recreated labels and equality diagonal, but removed original colored sector shading and arrow design; not a verified pixel reproduction.

training_pair.instruction: Using source metadata and data.csv, build a industry_scatter reusable chart with observed/digitized value provenance and source/neutral themes.
training_pair.response: Exact reproducible code is the immutable chart.py in this bundle; actual inputs are data.csv and config.json. Run `python chart.py --data data.csv --config config.json --theme source --output source.png` and repeat with neutral theme. Do not treat editorial redesign as original-image fidelity.
